title.en: Granted, admittedly, be that as it may
title.es: Concedido, eso sí, sea como sea

es: Reconocer marcadores de concesión C1 (granted, admittedly, be that as it may, that said, even so) y localizar la réplica que sigue en un debate.

vocabulary.es: es cierto, lo admito (abre una concesión)

teaching.en: Granted, the plan has a drawback, but it is still useful.
teaching.es: Es cierto que el plan tiene un inconveniente, pero sigue siendo útil.
teaching.explanationEs: Granted + coma reconoce un punto ajeno; la réplica llega después con but.
segments: Granted, the plan has a drawback,
but it is still useful.
teaching.audioText: Granted, the plan has a drawback, but it is still useful.

teaching.en: Admittedly, the price is high, but the service is excellent.
teaching.es: Hay que admitir que el precio es alto, pero el servicio es excelente.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly admite una debilidad; va al principio y la réplica viene después.
segments: Admittedly, the price is high,
but the service is excellent.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, the price is high, but the service is excellent.

teaching.en: Be that as it may, my opponent has not answered the question.
teaching.es: Sea como sea, mi oponente no ha respondido a la pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: Be that as it may abre la réplica sin but: ya marca el contraste por sí solo.
segments: Be that as it may, my
opponent has not answered the question.
teaching.audioText: Be that as it may, my opponent has not answered the question.

teaching.en: That said, the drawback is small.
teaching.es: Dicho esto, el inconveniente es pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: That said matiza lo que acabas de conceder y vuelve a tu conclusión.
segments: That said, the
drawback is small.
teaching.audioText: That said, the drawback is small.

teaching.en: The team lost the first point. Even so, it won the debate.
teaching.es: El equipo perdió el primer punto. Aun así, ganó el debate.
teaching.explanationEs: Even so va en la réplica, después de un punto que ya se ha concedido.
segments: The team lost the first point.
Even so, it won the debate.
teaching.audioText: The team lost the first point. Even so, it won the debate.

teaching.en: Admittedly, my opponent is right about the cost. That said, the benefits are bigger.
teaching.es: Hay que admitir que mi oponente tiene razón sobre el coste. Dicho esto, los beneficios son mayores.
teaching.explanationEs: Dos marcadores seguidos: primero concedes, después replicas con tu conclusión.
segments: Admittedly, my opponent is right about the
cost. That said, the benefits are bigger.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, my opponent is right about the cost. That said, the benefits are bigger.

prompt.es: Elige qué hace «granted» al empezar esta frase.

choices.text: It promises that the ticket is safe.
It gives the reason for the price.
It accepts a true point before the reply.

feedback.es: Granted reconoce un punto cierto (el precio alto) y la réplica llega con but; no significa «garantizado».

hint.es: Mira qué reconoce el hablante antes de la palabra but.

origin.text: Granted, the ticket is expensive, but the trip is worth it.

prompt.es: Completa: «El viaje es largo; aun así, vale la pena.»

feedback.es: Even so abre una réplica tras un punto concedido («el viaje es largo»): equivale a «aun así».

hint.es: Son dos palabras que abren una réplica y significan «aun así».

origin.text: The journey is long. ___, it is worth it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hay que admitir que el precio es alto, pero el servicio es bueno.»

answer.text: Admittedly the price is high but the service is good

feedback.es: Admittedly concede el punto débil (el precio) y but introduce la réplica a favor del servicio.

hint.es: Empieza con la palabra que admite el punto débil.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada marcador con lo que hace en un debate.

pairs: Granted, you are right about the price.

pairs.es: concede un punto del otro lado

pairs: Be that as it may, I disagree.
That said, it is still useful.

feedback.es: Cada marcador tiene su función: granted y admittedly conceden, y be that as it may y that said abren la réplica.

pairs: Granted, you are right about the price.

pairs.es: concede un punto del otro lado

pairs: Be that as it may, I disagree.
That said, it is still useful.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo reacciona la hablante ante el punto de su oponente.

choices.text: She accepts that the film is long but defends it.
She says the film is too long to enjoy.
She says her opponent has not seen the film.

feedback.es: «Granted, the film is very long» concede el punto; «But the story is so good…» es la réplica que defiende la película.

origin.audio: Granted, the film is very long. But the story is so good that I would watch it twice.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es cierto que es difícil, pero el equipo puede lograrlo.»

feedback.es: Admittedly (o granted) admite la dificultad al principio y but introduce la réplica.

origin.text: ___, it is difficult, but the team can do it.

prompt.es: Según la transcripción, ¿cuál es la réplica de Carlos tras su concesión?

choices.text: Phones can distract students.
Phones also help students find information fast.
Phones should be banned in class.

feedback.es: Carlos concede con «Granted, phones can distract» y su réplica, tras that said, es que los móviles ayudan a encontrar información.

origin.text:
Ana: We should ban phones in class.
Carlos: Granted, phones can distract students. That said, they also help students find information fast.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concede la hablante y qué defiende.

choices.text: She says her opponent has no experience at all.
She says experience always wins a debate.
She admits the other speaker has more experience but says it is not enough.

feedback.es: Admittedly concede la mayor experiencia del oponente y be that as it may abre la réplica: la experiencia sola no basta.

origin.audio: Admittedly, my opponent has more experience. Be that as it may, experience alone does not win a debate.

prompt.es: Elige el par de frases que concede un punto y luego replica con claridad.

choices.text: Granted, the hotel is noisy. Even so, the location is perfect.
The hotel is noisy, so the location is perfect.
The hotel is noisy, and so is the location.

feedback.es: Solo el primer par reconoce el ruido con granted y replica con even so; los otros no contraponen ideas.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hay que admitir que ganó, pero no me ha convencido.»

answer.text: Admittedly she won but she has not convinced me

feedback.es: Admittedly concede la victoria y but introduce la réplica: no me ha convencido.

prompt.es: Elige la réplica que sigue mejor a esta concesión.

choices.text: Therefore, the bus is much faster.
Even so, the bus is much cheaper.
Because of that, the train is cheaper.

feedback.es: Tras conceder que el tren es más rápido, even so opone el precio del autobús; las otras opciones no contrastan.

origin.text: Granted, the train is faster than the bus.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante del plan al final.

choices.text: She now believes the plan is perfect.
She wants a larger team to run the plan.
She accepts the earlier point but still thinks the plan is dangerous.

feedback.es: That said matiza lo concedido antes y la hablante mantiene su conclusión: el plan sigue siendo peligroso.

origin.audio: That said, I still think the plan is too dangerous for a small team.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me equivoqué; sea como sea, me sigue gustando la idea.»

feedback.es: Después de reconocer el error, be that as it may abre la réplica sin necesidad de but.

origin.text: I was wrong. ___, I still like the idea.

es: Usar hence, thereby, in so doing y whereby para expresar consecuencia y medio en registro formal.

vocabulary.es: por el cual, mediante el cual

teaching.en: The council introduced a fee; hence the drop in traffic.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento introdujo una tarifa; de ahí el descenso del tráfico.
teaching.explanationEs: Hence + nombre (o una oración) da la consecuencia; es formal y se usa al escribir.
segments: The council introduced a fee;
hence the drop in traffic.
teaching.audioText: The council introduced a fee; hence the drop in traffic.

teaching.en: The council charges a fee to discourage drivers, thereby reducing traffic.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento cobra una tarifa para desalentar a los conductores, con lo cual reduce el tráfico.
teaching.explanationEs: Thereby + verbo en -ing expresa el resultado o el medio de la acción anterior.
segments: The council charges a fee to
discourage drivers, thereby reducing traffic.
teaching.audioText: The council charges a fee to discourage drivers, thereby reducing traffic.

teaching.en: The council created a scheme whereby residents pay half the fee.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento creó un plan por el cual los residentes pagan la mitad de la tarifa.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereby (= by which) presenta el sistema o la regla con la que algo funciona.
segments: The council created a scheme whereby
residents pay half the fee.
teaching.audioText: The council created a scheme whereby residents pay half the fee.

teaching.en: The council lowered the fee. In so doing, it won support.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento bajó la tarifa. Al hacerlo, ganó apoyo.
teaching.explanationEs: In so doing retoma la acción anterior y da su resultado; el sujeto es el mismo.
segments: The council lowered the fee. In
so doing, it won support.
teaching.audioText: The council lowered the fee. In so doing, it won support.

teaching.en: The scheme is cheap to run, hence its popularity.
teaching.es: El plan es barato de gestionar; de ahí su popularidad.
teaching.explanationEs: Hence puede ir delante de un nombre sin verbo: hence its popularity.
segments: The scheme is cheap to
run, hence its popularity.
teaching.audioText: The scheme is cheap to run, hence its popularity.

teaching.en: The fee pays for new buses, thereby helping commuters.
teaching.es: La tarifa paga autobuses nuevos, con lo cual ayuda a quienes viajan a diario.
teaching.explanationEs: Thereby helping: la ayuda es la consecuencia directa de pagar los autobuses.
segments: The fee pays for new
buses, thereby helping commuters.
teaching.audioText: The fee pays for new buses, thereby helping commuters.

prompt.es: Elige el conector que completa la consecuencia con -ing.

choices.text: thereby
hence
whereby

feedback.es: Solo thereby se construye con un verbo en -ing (reducing); hence va con un nombre y whereby con una oración.

hint.es: Fíjate en que la palabra siguiente termina en -ing.

origin.text: The council raised the fee, ___ reducing traffic.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es un plan por el cual los conductores pagan una vez al mes.»

feedback.es: Whereby presenta el sistema («por el cual») y va seguido de una oración completa con sujeto y verbo.

hint.es: Equivale a «by which» y se escribe en una sola palabra.

origin.text: It is a scheme ___ drivers pay once a month.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El tráfico bajó; de ahí el aire más limpio.»

answer.text: Traffic fell hence the cleaner air

feedback.es: Hence se coloca justo antes del nombre que expresa la consecuencia: the cleaner air.

hint.es: Coloca hence justo antes de la consecuencia.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada conector formal con su uso.

pairs: Prices fell; hence the shorter queues.

pairs.es: hence: va con un nombre o una oración

pairs: The fee rose, thereby cutting traffic.

pairs.es: thereby: va con un verbo en -ing

pairs: A scheme whereby students share books.

pairs.es: whereby: presenta un sistema, «por el cual»

pairs: It saved money. In so doing, it helped families.

pairs.es: in so doing: retoma la acción anterior

feedback.es: Cada conector tiene su estructura: hence con nombre, thereby con -ing, whereby con oración e in so doing al empezar frase.

pairs: Prices fell; hence the shorter queues.

pairs.es: hence: va con un nombre o una oración

pairs: The fee rose, thereby cutting traffic.

pairs.es: thereby: va con un verbo en -ing

pairs.es: whereby: presenta un sistema, «por el cual»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué consigue la escuela con su nuevo plan.

choices.text: Students buy new books, so costs go up.
Students share books, so costs go down.
The school sells its books to the council.

feedback.es: «Whereby students share books» explica el sistema y «thereby reducing costs» el resultado: los costes bajan.

origin.audio: The school created a scheme whereby students share books, thereby reducing costs.

prompt.es: Completa: «Bajaron la tarifa; al hacerlo, ganaron apoyo.»

feedback.es: In so doing abre la frase siguiente y retoma la acción anterior (bajar la tarifa).

origin.text: They lowered the fee. ___, they won support.

prompt.es: Une las dos ideas del texto con una frase formal correcta.

choices.text: The city built new bike lanes, thereby to reduce car use.
The city built new bike lanes, whereby reducing car use.
The city built new bike lanes, thereby reducing car use.

feedback.es: Thereby pide un verbo en -ing; to reduce y whereby + -ing son errores de estructura.

origin.text: Idea 1: The city built new bike lanes. Idea 2: Car use went down.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la consecuencia que anuncia el alcalde.

choices.text: The number of bus passengers has gone up.
The number of bus passengers has gone down.
Bus fares will rise next year.

feedback.es: Hence introduce la consecuencia de la rebaja de tarifas: hence the increase in passengers significa que hay más pasajeros.

origin.audio: The mayor has lowered bus fares; hence the increase in passengers.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los buses son gratis los domingos; de ahí las multitudes.»

feedback.es: Hence va delante de un nombre (the crowds) y expresa la consecuencia de que los buses sean gratis.

origin.text: Buses are free on Sundays; ___ the crowds in the centre.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es un sistema por el cual los vecinos votan cada año.»

answer.text: It is a system whereby residents vote every year

feedback.es: Whereby presenta el sistema y le sigue una oración completa: residents vote every year.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta en registro formal.

choices.text: The fee is high; hence that traffic falls.
The fee is high; hence the fall in traffic.
The fee is high; thereby the fall in traffic.

feedback.es: Hence va con un nombre (the fall) sin that; thereby necesita un verbo en -ing.

origin.text: Quieres decir: «La tarifa es alta; de ahí la caída del tráfico.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo consigue ahorrar agua el hotel.

choices.text: Guests pay more, so the hotel saves money.
The hotel washes the towels every day.
Guests reuse their towels, so the hotel uses less water.

feedback.es: El sistema es reutilizar toallas y el resultado, con thereby saving, es usar menos agua.

origin.audio: The hotel introduced a scheme whereby guests reuse towels, thereby saving water.

prompt.es: Completa: «Reciclamos el papel; así reducimos los residuos.»

feedback.es: Thereby une la acción (reciclar papel) con su resultado en -ing: reducing waste.

origin.text: We recycle paper, ___ reducing waste.

title.es: Seguir un debate a dos voces

es: Seguir un debate breve y construir un mapa con argumento, contraargumento, concesión y cierre.

teaching.en: The moderator reads the motion and gives each speaker two minutes.
teaching.es: La moderadora lee la moción y da dos minutos a cada orador.
teaching.explanationEs: El moderador dirige el debate; la moción es la frase que se discute.
segments: The moderator reads the motion and
gives each speaker two minutes.
teaching.audioText: The moderator reads the motion and gives each speaker two minutes.

teaching.en: The motion is that homework should stop, and Tom is in favour of it.
teaching.es: La moción es que los deberes deberían terminar, y Tom está a favor.
teaching.explanationEs: In favour of = a favor de; against = en contra de.
segments: The motion is that homework should stop,
and Tom is in favour of it.
teaching.audioText: The motion is that homework should stop, and Tom is in favour of it.

teaching.en: Ana is against the motion, and her main argument is that students need practice.
teaching.es: Ana está en contra de la moción y su argumento principal es que los estudiantes necesitan práctica.
teaching.explanationEs: Against va sin preposición detrás: against the motion.
segments: Ana is against the motion, and her
main argument is that students need practice.
teaching.audioText: Ana is against the motion, and her main argument is that students need practice.

teaching.en: Tom's counterargument is that homework is tiring and takes too much time.
teaching.es: El contraargumento de Tom es que los deberes cansan y quitan demasiado tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: El contraargumento responde a lo que dijo el otro orador.
segments: Tom's counterargument is that homework is
tiring and takes too much time.
teaching.audioText: Tom's counterargument is that homework is tiring and takes too much time.

teaching.en: The moderator asks each speaker for a closing statement.
teaching.es: La moderadora pide a cada orador una declaración de cierre.
teaching.explanationEs: Closing statement: la frase final donde cada orador resume su postura.
segments: The moderator asks each speaker
for a closing statement.
teaching.audioText: The moderator asks each speaker for a closing statement.

teaching.en: To sum up, the motion divides the class: some want rules and some want a ban.
teaching.es: En resumen, la moción divide a la clase: unos quieren normas y otros una prohibición.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up abre el resumen final; es la señal del cierre.
segments: To sum up, the motion divides the class:
some want rules and some want a ban.
teaching.audioText: To sum up, the motion divides the class: some want rules and some want a ban.

prompt.es: Elige la pieza del mapa que expresa esta frase de Tom.

choices.text: An opening argument
A counterargument
A closing statement

feedback.es: «On the other hand» responde a lo que dijo otro orador: es un contraargumento.

hint.es: Fíjate si la frase responde a alguien o abre una postura.

origin.text: Ana: On the other hand, practice helps students remember.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom está a favor de la moción.»

feedback.es: In favour of es la expresión fija para «a favor de».

hint.es: Piensa en la frase fija que significa «a favor de».

origin.text: Tom is in ___ of the motion.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi argumento principal es que los deberes quitan demasiado tiempo.»

answer.text: My main argument is that homework takes too much time

feedback.es: My main argument is that… abre la postura y da la razón: homework takes too much time.

hint.es: Empieza con la señal que presenta el argumento.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada señal del debate con la pieza del mapa.

feedback.es: Cada señal marca una pieza: argumento, contraargumento, concesión o cierre.

prompt.es: Escucha el resumen y elige la postura de Mia sobre los uniformes.

choices.text: She supports uniforms because they save time.
She is the moderator and stays neutral.
She opposes uniforms because students need to express themselves.

feedback.es: Mia está «against» la moción y su razón es que los estudiantes necesitan expresarse.

origin.audio: The motion is that schools should have uniforms. Mia is against it. She says students need to express themselves.

prompt.es: Completa: «En resumen, la moción divide a la clase.»

feedback.es: To sum up es la fórmula de cierre: «en resumen».

origin.text: To ___ up, the motion divides the class.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el argumento principal de Leo.

choices.text: Phones take students' attention away from the lesson.
Phones are too expensive for most families.
Phones help students work faster in class.

feedback.es: Leo dice «phones distract students during lessons»: su argumento es que los móviles quitan atención a la clase.

origin.audio: Sara, the moderator: The motion is that phones should be banned in classrooms. Leo, you are in favour. Leo: My main argument is that phones distract students during lessons.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué concede Ana y cuál es su réplica?

choices.text: She accepts that phones help students, but says they distract.
She accepts that phones distract, but says students use them to check facts.
She accepts that a ban is needed, but says students need rules.

feedback.es: Ana concede con granted que los móviles distraen y replica con that said que los estudiantes los usan para comprobar datos.

origin.text: Ana: Granted, phones can distract. That said, students also use them to check facts. A total ban is too strict.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concede Leo y qué mantiene.

choices.text: He admits teachers can watch every screen, but says phones are useful.
He admits he has no argument, so he supports Ana.
He admits phones help students check facts, but says teachers cannot control every screen.

feedback.es: Leo concede con admittedly que los móviles sirven para comprobar datos y con even so mantiene que ningún profesor puede vigilar todas las pantallas.

origin.audio: Leo: Admittedly, phones help students check facts. Even so, no teacher can watch every screen in the room.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿cómo cierra Sara el debate?

choices.text: She sums up both positions.
She votes for Leo's ban.
She asks Ana to start again.

feedback.es: Con «To sum up» Sara resume las dos posturas sin tomar partido: es el cierre del debate.

origin.text:
Ana: Then the school should set clear rules instead of a ban.
Sara (moderator): Thank you both. To sum up, Leo wants a ban, and Ana wants clear rules.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión del debate con su significado.

pairs.es: quien dirige los turnos de palabra

feedback.es: Estas cuatro expresiones organizan un debate: posturas, quien modera y la respuesta al argumento contrario.

pairs.es: quien dirige los turnos de palabra

prompt.es: Completa: «La moderadora dirige el debate.»

feedback.es: El moderador dirige el debate y reparte los turnos; no defiende ninguna postura.

origin.text: The ___ leads the debate and gives each speaker a turn.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace Mia con el punto de Carlos.

choices.text: She rejects the safety point completely.
She accepts the safety point but raises a problem for shops.
She agrees that shops should close.

feedback.es: Mia concede con admittedly que los carriles bici son más seguros y aporta un contraargumento: las tiendas pierden aparcamiento.

origin.audio: Carlos: My main argument is that bike lanes make streets safer. Mia: Admittedly, they do. Still, shops lose parking spaces, and that is a counterargument we cannot ignore.

es: Escribir una réplica cortés que concede dos puntos y los rebate con evidencia (I take your point, I would not deny that, nonetheless, while).

teaching.en: I take your point about sleep, but the evidence on grades is not clear.
teaching.es: Entiendo tu punto sobre el sueño, pero las pruebas sobre las notas no son claras.
teaching.explanationEs: I take your point concede con cortesía antes de rebatir.
segments: I take your point about sleep, but
the evidence on grades is not clear.
teaching.audioText: I take your point about sleep, but the evidence on grades is not clear.

teaching.en: I would not deny that teenagers are tired. Nonetheless, a later start causes problems for parents.
teaching.es: No negaría que los adolescentes están cansados. Aun así, empezar más tarde causa problemas a los padres.
teaching.explanationEs: I would not deny that + oración concede; nonetheless abre la réplica.
segments: I would not deny that teenagers are tired.
Nonetheless, a later start causes problems for parents.
teaching.audioText: I would not deny that teenagers are tired. Nonetheless, a later start causes problems for parents.

teaching.en: While a later start could help sleep, it would also end the day later.
teaching.es: Si bien empezar más tarde podría ayudar a dormir, también haría que el día terminara más tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: While + concesión, coma y réplica: no se añade but.
segments: While a later start could help sleep,
it would also end the day later.
teaching.audioText: While a later start could help sleep, it would also end the day later.

teaching.en: With respect, the evidence you quote comes from only one school.
teaching.es: Con el debido respeto, las pruebas que citas vienen de un solo colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: With respect suaviza el desacuerdo antes de una crítica.
segments: With respect, the evidence you quote
comes from only one school.
teaching.audioText: With respect, the evidence you quote comes from only one school.

teaching.en: To rebut this claim, look at schools that already use a new timetable.
teaching.es: Para rebatir esta afirmación, mira los colegios que ya usan un horario nuevo.
teaching.explanationEs: To rebut = para rebatir: respondes a una afirmación con datos.
segments: To rebut this claim, look at schools
that already use a new timetable.
teaching.audioText: To rebut this claim, look at schools that already use a new timetable.

teaching.en: Nonetheless, the bus timetable will not change this year.
teaching.es: Aun así, el horario de los autobuses no cambiará este año.
teaching.explanationEs: Nonetheless va al inicio de frase, con coma después.
segments: Nonetheless, the bus timetable will
not change this year.
teaching.audioText: Nonetheless, the bus timetable will not change this year.

prompt.es: Elige la concesión cortés a la postura de un compañero.

choices.text: You are wrong about sleep.
Sleep does not matter at all.
I take your point about sleep.

feedback.es: I take your point reconoce lo cierto de la postura de Tom sin atacarlo; las otras opciones lo niegan o lo desprecian.

hint.es: La concesión reconoce algo cierto sin atacar a Tom.

origin.text: Tom: Teenagers should sleep until nine, so school must start later.

prompt.es: Completa: «No negaría que los adolescentes están cansados.»

feedback.es: I would not deny that… es la fórmula cortés para conceder un punto cierto.

hint.es: Es el verbo que corresponde a «negar».

origin.text: I would not ___ that teenagers are tired.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Con el debido respeto, un colegio no es evidencia suficiente.»

answer.text: With respect one school is not enough evidence

feedback.es: With respect suaviza el desacuerdo y la crítica se dirige a la evidencia, no a la persona.

hint.es: Empieza con la fórmula que suaviza el desacuerdo.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula con su función en la réplica.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple una función: conceder, rebatir, suavizar o apoyar con datos.

prompt.es: Elige la réplica con la concesión y el contraargumento bien unidos.

choices.text: While the school day could start later, parents would still need to leave early.
While the school day could start later, but parents would still need to leave early.

answer.text: Dear Tom, thank you for your post. I take your point about sleep, and I would not deny that many teenagers are tired in the morning. Nonetheless, I do not think a later start is the best answer. First, the evidence is not clear: one school changed its timetable, but the grades stayed the same. With respect, one example is not enough to change every school. Second, while a later start could help students sleep, it would also end the day later. Many students have sports, jobs or lessons after school, and their parents cannot always collect them. Buses would also need new timetables, and that would cost the council more money. I agree that students should rest, but perhaps the school could start a little later, at half past eight, and keep the day the same length. In conclusion, I accept that sleep matters, yet I believe a smaller change would solve the problem without creating new ones. Best wishes, Ana

answer.text: Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars, for three reasons. First, the air is dirty, and children breathe it every day. Second, the streets are narrow, and cyclists and pedestrians are not safe. Third, the centre can be a place where people walk, shop and meet. Granted, some shops are worried, and I would not deny that deliveries are a real difficulty. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities is encouraging. Visitors stay longer on pedestrian streets, hence the rise in sales reported by several shops. The council could also create a scheme whereby delivery vans enter before nine in the morning, thereby protecting both business and safety. With respect, a few parking spaces are a small price for cleaner air and safer streets. On balance, I believe the plan helps residents, visitors and shops. To sum up, we should protect the centre for people, not for cars. Thank you.
accepted: Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars, for three reasons. First, the air is dirty, and children breathe it every day. Granted, some shops are worried, and I would not deny that deliveries are a real difficulty. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities is encouraging. Visitors stay longer on pedestrian streets, hence the rise in sales reported by several shops. The council could also create a scheme whereby delivery vans enter before nine in the morning, thereby protecting both business and safety. With respect, a few parking spaces are a small price for cleaner air and safer streets. On balance, I believe the plan helps residents, visitors and shops. To sum up, we should protect the centre for people, not for cars. Thank you.

Good evening, everyone. I am against closing the whole centre to cars, and I have two main reasons. First, many older residents and sick people need to arrive by car. Second, shops need deliveries and customers who come from outside the city. Admittedly, the air in the centre is not clean, and I take your point about cyclists and pedestrians. Be that as it may, a full ban is too strict. The council could create a scheme whereby only electric vehicles enter at certain hours, thereby reducing pollution without closing the streets. Some cities tried a complete ban, hence the complaints from shops and the return of the old rules. With respect, the evidence is not as clear as my opponent says. That said, I would support a trial in one street first. On balance, a careful plan is better than a sudden ban. To sum up, we can protect both clean air and local shops. Thank you.
